provisions: Banned all on-premise drink discounts by any licensee under M.G.L. c. 138: no free drinks; no drinks below the price regularly charged during the same calendar week; no unlimited drinks for a fixed price; no single-day-only prices; pitchers only to 2+ persons; no larger pours without proportionate price increase; no drinking games or alcohol-as-prizes; no advertising of any prohibited practice
source: https://www.mass.gov/doc/204-cmr-4-prohibition-of-certain-practices/download (current text of 204 CMR 4.03); Colin Campbell, "Happy Hour Ban Starts in Massachusetts Bars," New York Times, Dec. 11, 1984
notes: Enactment date (promulgated Nov. 21, 1984) from Jeff Jacoby op-ed jeffjacoby.com/27915 (secondary); effective December 1984 per NYT — exact day not verified. Trigger: death of Kathleen Barry, Sept. 1983. CONFLICT: a 2011 capitolfax.com recap says Dukakis 'signed the happy hour ban' (implying a statute); contemporaneous NYT and ABCC materials describe a commission regulation, not a statute.

provisions: Prohibited specific sales practices by (a) licensed clubs — private clubs were the only liquor-by-the-drink licensees in 1985; drinking establishments were not created until 1987 — and (b) on-premise cereal malt beverage (3.2% beer) retailers: no free drinks; no drinks below acquisition cost; no unlimited drinks for a fixed price; no drink sold below the price charged other purchasers that day (the time-of-day/'happy hour' provision, later repealed 2012); no supersized pours without proportionate price increase; no drinking games/alcohol prizes; no advertising of prohibited practices. Not a blanket ban on all discounts.
source: https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch41/041_027_0022.html (history: 'L. 1985, ch. 173, § 5'); https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch41/041_026_0040.html (history: 'L. 1985, ch. 173, § 4'); Kansas Legislative Research Dept. liquor-laws timeline, https://kgi.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/api/collection/p16884coll8/id/294/download (1985 entry: 'Happy hour ban enacted')
notes: Enactment/effective month and day not verified; effective upon publication/July 1, 1985 assumed, not confirmed. 1985 scope confirmed: applied to private clubs and 3.2% beer retailers only (no general bar license class yet existed). Provision text reconstructed from the statute as amended through 2012.

provisions: Banned (1) selling alcoholic beverages during a portion of the day at a price reduced from the usual/customary/established price charged during the rest of that day — all-day specials remained legal; (2) furnishing 2+ servings for one order (2-for-1); (3) single price for required purchase of 2+ servings. Applied to holders of retailer's permits and to private clubs (not private functions closed to the public). Exception for price increases during paid live entertainment. Violation = Class B misdemeanor.
source: https://law.justia.com/codes/indiana/2011/title7-1/article5/chapter10/ (code text with history note 'As added by P.L.86-1985, SEC.2. Amended by P.L.79-1986, SEC.5.')
notes: It was a statute, not an ATC rule. Effective date not verified — presumed July 1, 1985 (Indiana standard), not confirmed. Amended by P.L.79-1986, §5; repealed effective July 1, 2024 (HEA 1086).

provisions: On-premise permittees/agents may not: sell more than one drink for a single price; set a single price conditioned on buying multiple drinks; deliver more than one drink at a time to one patron; give away or sell a drink at a non-usual price for less than a full business day; offer free or reduced drinks to a population segment (must be offered to all customers). Exceptions: pitchers for two or more patrons; single carafe or bottle of wine for one patron; packages including a meal or entertainment.
source: NC Office of Administrative Hearings rule PDF, history note 'Eff. August 1, 1985', http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2014b%20-%20public%20safety/chapter%2015%20-%20alcoholic%20beverage%20control%20commission/subchapter%20b/14b%20ncac%2015b%20.0223.pdf ; ND Insider, 'Why happy hour is banned in North Carolina,' 2021-11-17, https://www.ndinsider.com/story/news/2021/11/17/why-happy-hour-banned-north-carolina-law-restaurants-alcohol-bars/6037393001/
notes: Enactment (adoption/filing) date not found online; effective date from official history note. Classified strict ban because all time-limited drink-price reductions are prohibited, though full-business-day specials and meal/entertainment packages remain lawful.

provisions: Amendment to 04 NCAC 02S .0232, effective 1992-07-01. Official history confirms the amendment but no public source details its substance; the NC ABC Commission's 'Happy Hour FAQs' quotes Rule 2S.0232(d)-(e) as permitting meal/entertainment package offerings tied to New Year's, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, or Father's Day, suggesting the 1992 amendment added those package-offering exceptions.
source: Same OAH rule PDF (history note 'Amended Eff. ... July 1, 1992'); NC ABC Commission 'Happy Hour Frequently Asked Questions', https://b5d7ac.staticwbm.com/20220819232905/https://portal.abc.nc.gov/Public%20Web%20Documents/Divisions/Education/Publications/1.%20General%20Questions/Happy%20Hour%20Frequently%20Asked%20Questions.pdf
notes: Substance of the 1992 amendment not verifiable from public sources; the holiday-package link is an inference, not confirmed by rulemaking text.

provisions: Advertising rule 14B NCAC 15B .1004(g): no on-premise permittee or agent may advertise any drink promotion prohibited by .0223, including '2 for 1,' 'buy 1 get 1 free,' 'buy 1 get another for a (nickel, penny, etc.),' and any similar statement indicating a patron must buy more than one drink.
source: NC OAH rule PDF, history note 'Eff. January 1, 1982; Amended Eff. ... July 1, 1992; August 1, 1985; May 1, 1984', http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2014b%20-%20public%20safety/chapter%2015%20-%20alcoholic%20beverage%20control%20commission/subchapter%20b/14b%20ncac%2015b%20.1004.pdf
notes: The 1985-08-01 amendment coincided exactly with adoption of the happy-hour rule and the 1992-07-01 amendment with its amendment, suggesting coordinated changes; which amendment introduced the 2-for-1 ad-ban language could not be verified.

provisions: R.I. Gen. Laws § 3-7-26: licensees and employees/agents may not require purchase of multiple drinks through a reduced price; increase alcoholic volume without a proportionate price increase; offer unlimited drinks for a fixed price during a set period; hold drinking games/promotions or award alcohol prizes for on-premise consumption; or advertise/promote happy hours, open bars, two-for-one nights, or free-drink specials. Exceptions: free food or entertainment; alcohol in meal packages; wine by bottle or carafe with meals or for more than one person; free wine tastings. Does not otherwise limit the price charged for a drink. Compliance is a condition of every on-premise license.
source: Official RI statute page, http://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE3/3-7/3-7-26.htm ; S & S Liquor Mart, Inc. v. Pastore, 497 A.2d 729 (R.I. 1985, decided 1985-08-26), https://law.justia.com/cases/rhode-island/supreme-court/1985/497-a-2d-729.html ; Justia codified history ('Enacted by P.L. 1985, ch. 345, section 1'), https://law.justia.com/codes/rhode-island/2022/title-3/chapter-3-7/section-3-7-26/
notes: Exact passage, approval, and effective day of P.L. 1985, ch. 345 not verifiable online (original session-law text not found); the 1985-08-26 Supreme Court opinion proves the act was in force by then. REJECTED dates: listicles claiming 1989, and an archive reference loosely associating RI with 1984 (likely a Massachusetts conflation). Next statutory amendment in 1996 (outside period); no other statewide changes 1980-1995.

provisions: Liquor Control Board General Regulation 49 (recodified as General Regulation 43; current citation 26-001 Code Vt. R. 26-020-001-X): first-class and first+third-class licensees may not offer alcohol at reduced prices for any period of time during daily legal hours; may not conduct games, contests, or promotions encouraging rapid or excessive consumption or furnish alcohol free of charge. Exceptions: group events (banquets) open to attendees only, cover charges, certain live-entertainment price adjustments; reduced prices lasting the full business day remain lawful.
citation: Liquor Control Board General Regulation 49 (recodified as General Regulation 43; current: 26-001 Code Vt. R. 26-020-001-X)
source: Cornell LII regulation page, https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/vermont/26-001-Code-Vt-R-26-020-001-X ; VT LCAR 14-P02 annotated rule text (2014-03-06), https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2014/WorkGroups/LCAR/14-P02%20-%20Regulations%20Related%20to%20the%20Sale%20of%20Alcoholic%20Liquor/W~Department%20of%20Liquor%20Control~14-P02%20-%20Annotated%20Text%20of%20Rule~3-6-2014.pdf ; Reason, Aug.-Sept. 1986, https://reason.com/1986/08/01/green-mountain-blues/printer/
notes: Original adoption year and effective date could not be verified online. A February 1986 quotation shows 'bills banning happy hours' under consideration in the Vermont House, consistent with a mid-1980s regulatory ban, but does not establish the Board's adoption or effective date. Vermont SOS online rulemaking records cover filings only from August 14, 2018 onward; the LCAR packet gives no adoption history.

provisions: Statewide ban on happy hours/time-limited drink specials for all retail licensees: mandatory drink-price schedules (no intraday changes); no serving 2+ drinks at once to one person; no unlimited drinks for a fixed price (except private functions); no one-day reduced prices promoting consumption; no disproportionate volume/size increases; no drinking games/contests; no advertising of these. All-day specials remained legal.
citation: 235 ILCS 5/6-28 (from Ch. 43, par. 144d), Liquor Control Act of 1934
source: NHTSA Digest of State Alcohol Highway Safety Related Legislation, 12th ed. (current 1/1/1994), https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/Impaired_Driving/Impaired_Driving_Digests/12th%20Edition%201994.pdf ; pre-2015 text of §6-28 quoted in 2006 IL Senate Amendment 1 to SB 948, https://trackbill.com/s3/bills/IL/94/SB/948/amendments/senate-amendment-001.pdf
notes: Exact 1989 public-act number, approval date, and effective date not found via public web search; year-only dates used. Secondary sources consistently date the ban to 1989 (one source said 'around 1985,' rejected). Relaxed by P.A. 99-46 (2015), outside the study window.

provisions: No licensee may advertise or offer 'happy hours,' except between 4 p.m. and 7 p.m., or any other means or inducements to stimulate consumption of alcoholic beverages, including: no more than two drinks to one person at once; no drinks below the price regularly charged that calendar week (except private functions); no unlimited drinks for a fixed price (except private functions); no below-public-price or volume-manipulation schemes; no drinking games or drink prizes.
citation: Laws 1985, c. 6, § 34 (HB 1118, 40th Leg., Oklahoma Alcoholic Beverage Control Act), codified at 37 O.S. §537; cited as §537(B)(4) by NHTSA digest current 1/1/1994
source: Justia Oklahoma §37-537 history note ('Amended by Laws 1985, c. 6, § 34, emerg. eff. March 14, 1985'), https://law.justia.com/codes/oklahoma/2015/title-37/section-37-537/ ; OK AG Op. 85-52, https://www.casemine.com/judgement/us/59148e6eadd7b04934553dda ; 2011 HB 1354 ENGR quoting the provision, https://www.oklegislature.gov/cf_pdf/2011-12%20ENGR/hB/HB1354%20ENGR.PDF
notes: State Question 563 (approved 1984-09-18) authorized county-option liquor by the drink; HB 1118 implemented it — the ban was tied to liquor-by-the-drink legalization as expected. CONFLICT: whether the 4-7 p.m. happy-hour carve-out was original to the 1985 act or added later is unresolved (a circa-2001 UDETC summary quotes the provision without it; 2011 legislative text includes it).

source: NHTSA Digest of State Alcohol Highway Safety Related Legislation, 12th ed. (current 1/1/1994): 'Anti-Happy Hour Laws/Regulations: No,' https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/Impaired_Driving/Impaired_Driving_Digests/12th%20Edition%201994.pdf
notes: ANSWER TO PRE-2011 QUESTION: no qualifying statewide anti-happy-hour law/regulation in 1980-1995. License-specific pricing restrictions (no discount/2-for-1/unlimited/free-drink promotions, no time-limited 'happy hour' prices) verifiably existed pre-2011 for private clubs (Utah Code §32A-5-107), banquet licensees, and limited restaurants (2004 enrolled SB 58; 2006 Utah Code), but their first-enactment date could not be established and may postdate 1995. The comprehensive statewide ban on drink specials (uniform price; no time-limited 'happy hour' prices) came with the 2011 recodification, Title 32B-5-305, effective 2011-07-01 — outside the study window. Conflicting secondary claims listed both: some describe 2011 as Utah's first happy-hour ban; 2012 commentary indicates 2011 broadened existing restrictions.

provisions: No licensee shall sell, or serve for on-premises consumption, an unlimited quantity of beer, wine, or spirits at a specific price; LCC characterizes violations as 'Multiple drinks for one price' / 'Bottomless' drinks under Rules and Regulations Chapter 6.
citation: 237 Neb. Admin. Code, ch. 6, § 019.01U1 (Neb. LCC Rules and Regulations, Ch. 6)
source: https://lcc.nebraska.gov (LCC homepage: 'Multiple drinks for one price' / 'Bottomless' drinks violate the Act and Chapter 6 rules); https://docsbay.net/doc/808566/Drink-Special-Prohibitions-in-State-Statute-Or-Administrative-Rule (50-state survey quoting 019.01U1)
notes: Adoption and effective dates not found in any public source; restriction verified only in current/undated sources, so placement in 1980-1995 is UNCONFIRMED. No tightening, loosening, or repeal found through 1995.

provisions: Banned requiring or allowing patrons to pre-purchase more than one drink (tickets, tokens, admission fees, 'two-for-one' or similar) as a condition of entry, service, or entertainment; banned free drinks, gifts, prizes, or anything of value conditioned on alcohol purchase; barred increased drink size without corresponding price treatment and multiple-drink/all-you-can-drink offers. Half-price single drinks remained permitted; below-cost sales barred separately under N.J.A.C. 13:2-24.8.
source: NJ ABC Bulletin 2381, opinion letter 1980-10-16, https://dspace.njstatelib.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/317c3fe2-7340-44a0-8843-be46ce5426fd/content ; NJ ABC Handbook, https://dspace.njstatelib.org//bitstream/10929/27277/1/nj_kfn_2175_a81_2011.pdf
notes: No amendment, tightening to a full ban, loosening, or repeal found 1980-1995. One secondary blog asserts the rule was created in 1980 and last substantively amended in 2006 (unverified).

provisions: On-premises licensees barred from selling, offering, or advertising an unlimited quantity of alcoholic liquor at a specific price; barred from selling 2 or more identical drinks for 1 price (second and additional identical drinks must cost the same as the first).
source: MLCC Code and Rules (history: 1979 ACS 16 Eff. Nov. 15 1983; 1985 MR 1 Eff. Feb. 13 1985), https://AnnArborChronicle.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/04/MLCC_Code_and_Rules_343265_7.pdf
notes: Unclear which clause(s) were in the original 1983 rule versus added by the 1985 amendment (see next row). No full ban, loosening, or repeal found through 1995.

provisions: Rule 38 as amended (1985 Annual Administrative Code Supplement); substance of amendment not verified — may have added the two-or-more-identical-drinks clause or been technical/reorganizational.
notes: Amendment effective date per rule history (1985 MR 1). No contemporaneous Michigan Register text located to confirm what changed.

provisions: Barred: (a) 2+ servings on an order for one serving; (b) unlimited servings for a fixed price over a set period; (c) sales below the monthly posted price schedule after 9 p.m.; (d) drinking games or alcohol prizes; (e) larger drink volume without proportionate price increase. Monthly price schedule required; discounts below schedule allowed only before 9 p.m. ('happy hour periods').
source: https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-administrative-code/rule-4301:1-1-50 (prior effective dates 4/15/1988, 9/20/1988); DDDJ, Inc. v. Ohio Liquor Control Comm., 64 Ohio App.3d 828 (1990), https://www.ahcuah.com/lawsuit/newsuit/ohio/dddj.htm
notes: CONFLICT with the 'by early 1985' premise: official OAC history gives 4/15/1988 as the first effective date for 4301:1-1-50 (corroborated by a 1990 court decision enforcing it for 8/11/1988 violations), but a contemporaneous 1985-02-07 Alaska Senate memo lists Ohio among states that had already 'outlawed similar forms of liquor promotion' — suggesting a pre-1988 restriction under a citation not located. No tightening, loosening, or repeal found through 1995.

provisions: TABC rule ended two-for-one drinks; bars could still reduce the price of individual drinks or serve double shots in one glass (per March 1985 reporting). Modern codification (16 TAC 45.103) is broader: bans undetermined-quantity/fixed-price service, buy-in pricing, consumption-based pricing, discounts after 11 p.m., serving more than two drinks at once, low-price cover-charge schemes, consumption contests/alcohol prizes, and practices inducing excess consumption.
citation: TABC on-premises promotions rule (modern codification: 16 Tex. Admin. Code 45.103)
source: D Magazine, March 1985 (contemporaneous), https://www.dmagazine.com/publications/d-magazine/1985/march/happy-hour-ban-difficult-to-swallow/ ; TABC bulletin (current rule summary), https://www.tabc.texas.gov/static/sites/default/files/2020-06/mpb-012a.pdf
notes: In effect by March 1985 per D Magazine; exact 1984-85 rule number and effective date not found. Rep. Gary Thompson's 1985 bill (69th Legislature) to also ban cut-rate drinks, contests, and special promotions was pending in March 1985; outcome not verified. Later additions to 45.103 (e.g., 11 p.m. discount cutoff) not dated; no repeal found through 1995.

source: Current: 4 DE Admin. Code 908 (formerly ABC Rule 2), https://archive.regulations.delaware.gov/AdminCode/title4/900/908.pdf ; 2016 final order, https://archive.regulations.delaware.gov/register/february2016/final/19%20DE%20Reg%20775%2002-01-16.pdf
notes: No statewide happy-hour/drink-special law change could be verified for 1980-1995. A statewide partial restriction exists today (4 DE Admin. Code 908, formerly ABC Rule 2: bans free drinks, below-cost sales, consumption-conditioned events, 2+ drinks for the price of one, and unlimited drinks for a set price), but the 2016 final order gives no original adoption date, and no session law, register entry, or contemporaneous source dates the restriction to 1980-1995.

provisions: Prohibited all liquor licensees, employees and agents from: (1) serving free drinks; (2) delivering more than 2 drinks to one person at one time; (3) selling unlimited drinks for a fixed price, except private functions not open to the public; (4) conducting drinking games/contests or awarding drinks as prizes; (5) any other practice specifically intended to encourage excessive drinking; and (6) advertising or promoting these practices. Exceptions included free food/entertainment, drinks in meal packages, wine by bottle/carafe with meals or to more than one person, wine tastings, hotel room service, reduced prices for prearranged private parties, and different prices in separate rooms.
notes: Approval date 1985-06-28 per official legislative history. Effective date 1985-09-19 is the session's general non-emergency effective date; c.492's own final page was not directly observed. Recodified without substantive change by PL 1987, c. 45 as 28-A MRSA §709 (effective 1987-09-29); not counted as a separate row. Listicles describing Maine as having a full ban of unknown date are contradicted by this primary record.

provisions: Amended the happy-hour exception (28-A MRSA §709) to cover 'wine, malt liquor or mixed drinks by the bottle, carafe or pitcher when sold with meals or to more than one person,' expanding the prior exception limited to 'wine by the bottle or carafe.' A substantive loosening of the restriction.
source: Current 28-A MRSA §709 text with inline section history, https://legislature.maine.gov/statutes/28/title28sec305-A.pdf ; PL 1987, c. 45 text, http://lldc.mainelegislature.org/Open/Laws/1987/1987_PL_c045.pdf
notes: Effective date 1987-09-29 is the session's general non-emergency effective date. Strike/add language taken from the delta between the c.45 text and the current §709 text; the c.342 session-law page itself was not opened.

provisions: Amended 28-A MRSA §709(1)(A)(2): the per-person delivery cap, previously 'more than 2 drinks,' was rewritten to prohibit delivering 'more than 2 drinks, or a pitcher of malt liquor or carafe of wine containing more than one liter or 33.8 ounces, to one person at one time.' A clarification/tightening extending the cap to large pitchers and carafes.
notes: Effective date 1993-10-13 is the general effective date for 1993 first-regular-session non-emergency laws. Signing/approval date not verified.

provisions: WAC 314-52-110(2): no retail licensee may offer liquor for on-premises consumption under advertising slogans such as 'two for the price of one,' 'two for one drinks,' 'buy one—get one free,' 'two for $__,' or any similar phrase/slogan whose express or implied meaning is that a customer must purchase more than one drink or quantity of liquor at one time to receive a reduced price. Statewide, all retail licensees.
citation: WSR 83-23-122 (Order 132, Resolution No. 141), amending WAC 314-52-110; authority RCW 66.08.030, 66.08.060, 66.98.070
source: 1990 WAC text and history note, https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/law/WACArchive/1990/WAC314.pdf ; 1977 WAC text (language absent), https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/law/WACArchive/1977/WAC314.pdf
notes: Filing date 1983-11-23 from the official WAC history note. Effective date 1983-12-24 derived (31 days after filing per the APA default), not individually confirmed. Residual uncertainty: the section was also amended in 1980 (80-09-078) and 1982 (82-17-031), whose texts were unavailable; the single-section 1983 filing is the most likely vehicle. Listicles claiming a 1989 Washington ban are contradicted by the WAC archives.

provisions: New WAC 314-52-114: no retail licensee may advertise, offer for sale, or sell beer, wine, or spirituous liquor at less than acquisition cost, with exceptions for closeouts/seasonal goods, damaged or deteriorating/perishable goods, court-ordered sales, and meeting a competitor's price. Statewide, all retail licensees.
source: 1990 WAC text and history note showing 83-24-060 as the original filing, https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/law/WACArchive/1990/WAC314.pdf
notes: Filing date 1983-12-07 from the official WAC history note. Effective date 1984-01-07 derived (31 days after filing per APA default), not individually confirmed. Amended 8/5/86 (86-16-060) and 1/29/87 (87-04-026); substance of those amendments not verified. Included as a drink-special restriction (general price floor).

provisions: No free promotional drinks; no drinks at reduced prices relative to the same week; no unlimited drinks for a fixed price; no pricing for select groups only; no serving a person already holding two drinks; no drinking games or drinks as prizes; no advertising of prohibited practices. Sponsor memo states 'the bill would eliminate happy hours.'
citation: SB 138, 14th Leg., 2d Sess. (1986), proposed new AS 04.16.015
source: https://www.akleg.gov/pdf/billfiles/Committee%20Bill%20Files/1985-1986%20-%2014th%20Legislature/SSTA%2014/SSTA14%20SB%20138.pdf ; https://www.akleg.gov/pdf/billfiles/Committee%20Bill%20Files/1985-1986%20-%2014th%20Legislature/SFIN/SFIN14%20SB%20138.pdf ; Senate State Affairs letter of intent 1986-02-20
notes: Bill files and letter of intent confirm the 1986 push and intended AS 04.16.015 text; current AS 04.16.015 retains equivalent restrictions. Final session-law chapter, approval date, and exact effective date not verified.

provisions: Title 40, Sec. 13.102 (PLCB): discount pricing limited to two consecutive hours before midnight; no two-for-one, no unlimited drinks for a fixed price; one specific alcoholic beverage per day may remain discounted all day.
notes: Effective 1985-12-27 per later reporting on the rule's history. A 2011 loosening (two-hour window extended to four hours) is outside the study period.

provisions: Sec. 30-6-A24b: no more than one drink at a time per person; no pitchers/multi-drink vessels except to two or more persons; no unlimited drinks for a fixed price; no drinking games or drinks as prizes; private functions and hotel guest bars exempt.
citation: Regs. of Conn. State Agencies Sec. 30-6-A24b
notes: Effective 1986-01-31 per UDETC history note; original 1986 adoption not independently verified against the regulation's own history.

provisions: Sec. 30-6-A24b amended 1995-03-03; substance of the amendment not verified from available sources.
citation: Regs. of Conn. State Agencies Sec. 30-6-A24b
notes: Amendment date confirmed; whether it tightened or loosened the rule is unresolved.

provisions: HRS Sec. 281-78.5: no on-premises licensee may engage in practices promoting excessive consumption of liquor; each liquor commission must adopt rules prohibiting specific promotion practices (e.g., all-you-can-drink for a fixed price, liquor-as-prize games).
citation: Act 137, 1987 Haw. Sess. Laws (SB 216), HRS Sec. 281-78.5
notes: Act effective upon approval. A Honolulu Liquor Commission 1986-87 annual report describes the Act as having 'rang the bell on happy hours and other promotions designed to promote excessive consumption.'

provisions: 3 VAC 5-50-160: no happy-hour discounts 9 p.m.-2 a.m.; max two drinks per person during happy hour; no two-for-one offers, pitchers of mixed drinks, giveaways, unlimited fixed-price drinks, or disproportionate volume increases; no external/media advertising of drink specials.
source: Rule text via UDETC: http://udetc.org/documents/HappyHoursDrinkSpecialsPolicies.pdf ; 'since 1985' on ad restriction: https://richmondbizsense.com/2012/02/09/a-happier-hour-ahead/ and http://rvanews.com/news/regulations-on-happy-hour-advertising-set-to-change
notes: CONFLICT: two secondary sources say the ad restriction has been effective 'since 1985,' while one AP-based article says the rule dates to 1984. Enactment date from primary regulatory history not verified.

provisions: 1985 Atlanta-area county action(s) reportedly in DeKalb, Cobb, and Fulton counties; ordinance number and text not independently located.
